title: Casual online play implementation backlog

parent.title: Implement casual online chess, player agents and public profiles

evidenceStatus: All 60 implementation scenarios remain not_run. This is a curated backlog snapshot, not implementation or acceptance evidence.

milestones.name: Public profiles, history and data removal

tickets.title: Preserve offline play and add draw/resign icon controls
tickets.outcome: The current offline game keeps its layout and behavior, with draw and resign available beside the existing board tools.
scope: Retain local setup, board, clocks, move sidebar, Undo, keyboard/history navigation and current model/engine behavior. Offline play must not depend on online sessions or transport.

Add the accepted draw icon and resign flag, with explicit result/confirmation behavior and fencing of pending local moves after a final result. Reuse local lifecycle semantics; do not invent a network draw protocol.
Use icons for existing actions whose meaning is clear. Keep accessible names, tooltips, visible focus and usable pointer/touch targets. Preserve meaningful settings labels and confirmation copy.
completionEvidence: Demonstrate offline human/model/engine flows, draw and resignation, pending-reply rejection, Undo and keyboard move review on the changed build.
Compare desktop and phone layouts with the existing game. Record focused regression and accessibility checks for the changed controls.

tickets.title: Add shared online state, transactional commands and operation receipts
tickets.outcome: Online matches have a versioned durable contract and one Go transaction writer, separate from private single-owner sync.
scope: Add additive PostgreSQL migrations and typed Go/TypeScript contracts for matches/seats, accepted events, immutable results, clocks/deadlines, queue entries, runner leases, public projections and deletion markers.

Define authenticated command intents, expected match version, seat/control epoch, operation ID and durable receipts. Reject changed payloads reusing an operation ID; repeat the original receipt after a lost acknowledgement.
Serialize acceptance against the current state. Sample decision time after lock acquisition, reconcile deadlines with that fresh time and commit candidate transitions only against the same version.
Keep provider credentials, raw requests, reasoning, private routes and owner-only archives outside shared state. Preserve the existing private sync schema/API and runtime-role isolation.
completionEvidence: Run real PostgreSQL migration and transaction tests, including competing writers, lost acknowledgements, payload mismatch and a lock wait crossing expiry.
Publish the shared contract and schema boundaries, with tests proving the private rules process cannot write canonical state.

tickets.title: Run the pinned chess rules in a private Node worker
tickets.outcome: The Go authority can evaluate online positions through the same pinned chessops/application policy used by local play.
scope: Wrap the pure modules in src/rules with a private versioned Node/TypeScript request/response process. Use the locked chessops dependency and existing October 18 rules amendment.
Cover strict FEN and counters, en passant, castling, promotions, repetition, mate/draw precedence, material and bounded timeout outcomes. Do not restore exhaustive interactive proof search.
Return candidates and the evaluated input/version to Go. Expose no public endpoint, database writer, provider credentials or private archives.
Provide one local start/build path and bounded worker-failure behavior suitable for later service recovery.
completionEvidence: Run browser/worker conformance fixtures across the listed rules and endings, including invalid FEN and boundary cases.
Show worker crash/timeout cannot commit a partial or stale match transition. Record dependency/license and packaging changes.

tickets.title: Authorize online participants and revocable guest seats
tickets.outcome: Only a current participant session can command or subscribe to its online seat.
scope: Extend the existing Clerk verification with match membership, seat, origin, expiry and revocation checks. Cancel stale client work when the signed-in identity changes.
Issue private revocable seat-scoped guest credentials on invitation acceptance. Support reconnect and verified guest removal requests without turning the public invitation into a control token.
Separate public invitation/replay reads from participant-only live state. A consumed link grants no seat control.
Define explicit proof of guest-seat ownership for account linking, without silently merging a guest into the current account.
completionEvidence: Exercise wrong owner/seat/origin, expired or revoked sessions, identity changes, consumed invitation replay and guest reconnect/removal credentials.
Demonstrate stream renewal rechecks authorization and no live participant data leaks through public routes.

tickets.title: Implement authoritative online moves, clocks and match outcomes
tickets.outcome: Both participants see one accepted move order, continuous clocks and one final result.
scope: Connect authenticated commands, the private rules candidate and the Go writer. Reject illegal, stale, wrong-seat and late moves; add increment exactly once per accepted move.
Implement first-move start and the 15-second opening reply abort for either starting side. Neither main bank runs before that side's first move; after the opening reply the next side's clock runs.
Before a side's own first-ever accepted move, cancellation aborts. Afterward it resigns, even if a takeback removed that move from the current line.
Implement mutual draw offers and exact-version takeback targets without refunding time or spent recovery budgets. Preserve discarded private archives and automatic draw rules.

Keep clocks running through generation, Stop/Retry, provider failure, control changes, navigation and peer disconnect. Reconcile expiry before accepting each intent; final results cannot be overwritten.
completionEvidence: Use deterministic time and actual PostgreSQL races for opening clocks, Black-to-move FEN, increment duplication, late moves and lock waits crossing expiry.
Verify stale offers, takebacks and late model replies cannot change a later position or final result. Record terminal-result and cancellation coverage.

tickets.title: Deliver finite authenticated updates with snapshot and polling recovery
tickets.outcome: Clients recover the current online state after dropped events, token renewal, tab changes or API restarts.
scope: Use direct authenticated HTTPS POST commands and fetch-SSE updates, with bounded polling fallback. Retain durable event cursors and canonical snapshots.
Limit each stream to at most 20 seconds or auth expiry. Acquire fresh credentials, send heartbeats and recheck membership on renewal.
Handle gaps, duplicates, slow readers and dropped acknowledgements without reapplying moves or regressing versions.
Release database connections while a stream is idle; preserve existing private sync behavior.
completionEvidence: Simulate cursor gaps, duplicate/lost events, slow readers, auth expiry, revoked membership and API restart.
Verify SSE renewal and poll fallback converge on the same snapshot and idle streams do not reserve a database connection.

tickets.title: Implement online presence and optional abandonment claims
tickets.outcome: A connected opponent may use the full clock; a continuous minute offline enables an optional win claim.
scope: Implement the approved five-second application heartbeat and 15-second liveness lease, with responsive background tabs eligible and suspended clients treated by lease state.
After both sides have moved and the opponent is continuously offline for 60 seconds, expose Claim win or Keep waiting. Waiting preserves the option and normal clock behavior.
Serialize reconnect, claim, clock expiry and normal endings. Reconnect accepted first clears eligibility; another disconnect starts a fresh minute.
Connected stalling never exposes a claim, including with the entire 20 minutes remaining. Consume the service-health boundary so a service outage cannot masquerade as opponent absence.
completionEvidence: Test connected stalling, lease expiry, 59/60-second boundaries, Keep waiting, reconnect/claim races and earlier terminal outcomes.
Show the claim is absent during service unavailability and cannot bypass the opening abort rules.

tickets.title: Recover online service interruptions without false abandonment results
tickets.outcome: API or rules-service interruption preserves prior results and resumes unfinished games with one canonical recovery adjustment.
scope: Persist planned suspension boundaries and durable health checkpoints for unexpected failures, using accepted activity to derive the conservative interruption interval.
Adjust unfinished active deadlines once according to the approved recovery contract; publish canonical state before accepting resumed actions.
Fence old service and runner epochs, invalidate stale work and preserve already final results.
Distinguish service unavailability from opponent offline presence in APIs and client state; retain original queue-cutoff recovery contracts.
completionEvidence: Inject crashes before/after commit, restart twice and replay recovery. Prove adjustments happen once and old replies cannot commit.
Verify service interruption awards no peer-abandonment win, preserves terminal games and converges across both clients.

tickets.title: Build public usernames, avatars and explicit guest linking
tickets.milestone: Public profiles, history and data removal
tickets.outcome: Accounts have a stable public profile identity without exposing their private sign-in identity.
scope: Add stable public profile IDs, editable unique usernames and chosen avatars, with ownership-checked updates and public reads.
Never default to Clerk email, legal name or authentication IDs in public payloads or historical participant labels.
Keep guests labeled Guest without a profile. Account linking is an explicit action that proves ownership of the guest seat.
Provide the username lookup needed by named friend challenges; preserve existing sign-in and private account controls.
completionEvidence: Test username uniqueness/edit races, avatar ownership and public payload allowlists.
Demonstrate signed-out profile reads and explicit verified guest linking, including rejection of another person's seat.

tickets.title: Run browser-owned online agents with turn leases and safe handoffs
tickets.outcome: One current browser runner controls an agent seat for each turn, while separately requested games can run concurrently.
scope: Reuse existing direct-provider adapters, model selection, history and classified-turn recovery. Keep credentials, private routes and conversations in the owner's browser.
Implement per-seat/per-turn runner leases and epochs. Duplicate tabs share the same game/entry; separate explicit games may use the same or different agents without an arbitrary owner cap.
Version human takeover, agent handoff and model/connection switches between accepted moves. Fence old provider replies and keep clocks and spent budgets.
Preserve four illegal attempts and the independent three automatic formatting corrections. Explicit model resignation concedes; transport failure alone does not.
After runner loss during uncertain billable work, offer explicit Retry, switch or takeover instead of automatically issuing another provider request.
completionEvidence: Use synthetic providers for duplicate tabs, simultaneous games, late replies, revoked leases, control switches and independent retry budgets.
Show exactly-once accepted moves, honest uncertain-request recovery and no credentials/private conversation in shared commands or replay data.

tickets.title: Build the online board workspace and concurrent-game navigation
tickets.outcome: Accepted structure A supports online play and parallel games while the existing offline game remains intact.
scope: Integrate canonical online snapshots, seats, clocks, reconnect status, results and control handoffs into the current Classic board/move workspace.
Add compact access to New play, concurrent Games and profile/history. Changing tabs/routes must not silently join another queue or lose a live game.

Use icon-only actions where meaning is clear, with accessible names, tooltips, visible focus and usable targets. Preserve the 20-word interface and 10-word engine-screen conventions, excluding game data.
Keep the separate Declared models per-move block absent. Show appropriate compact player/model identity, and keep review/simulation tooling out of production.
completionEvidence: Exercise multiple live games, identity changes, reconnect, control handoff, results and navigation using the integrated service.
Record desktop/phone layout, keyboard/focus and icon-label checks against accepted prototype commit 367ad78069571ff053002e1aaf74e8aad4bf1ec1.

tickets.title: Implement friend invitations, account challenges and mutual rematches
tickets.outcome: Two people can arrange a casual friend game as humans or through their own agents, including guests joining by link.
scope: Build one-use shareable links and account challenges, with 12-hour expiry, inviter cancellation and atomic consumption. Named challenges require accounts; link participants may be guests.
Each person chooses human or their own agent. The inviter chooses color, clock/increment and optional custom position, visible before acceptance.
Show public inviter name or Guest and the actual setup without inventing a final pairing. Do not offer a built-in Stockfish friend seat or a separate Ready approval step.
Connect acceptance to the canonical match and opening rules. Rematches require both participants, create a new game, reverse colors and retain setup unless changes are mutually agreed.
completionEvidence: Run guest/account combinations and human/human, human/agent and agent/agent flows with real APIs and synthetic provider execution.
Test expired/cancelled links, concurrent acceptance, invalid positions, named-recipient isolation and duplicate rematch acceptance.

tickets.title: Match compatible queue entries atomically at the ten-second cutoff
tickets.outcome: Each signed-in ready queue entry commits exactly one compatible game or the agreed fallback assignment.
scope: Require sign-in and explicit entry creation. Match different owners with identical starting time/increment and at least one agent seat, preferring the oldest eligible entry. Use random colors and the standard position.
Start the ten-second window on authoritative ready-entry acceptance, not during checks. Keep settings fixed; cancellation/rejoin after a change starts a fresh window.
Allow unlimited explicit concurrent entries/games. Opening the same entry in another tab creates no extra entry. Completing a game does not automatically requeue.
Serialize candidate selection, reservations, cancellation and engine fallback. A ready compatible candidate at exact cutoff equality wins; consume each entry once.

Resolve delayed deadline workers against original cutoffs and eligibility. Expire unresponsive waiting entries, require explicit rejoin and prevent late candidates or readiness from replacing an assigned opponent.
Support explicit Keep searching without an automatic cutoff and retry's final candidate recheck before fallback.
completionEvidence: Use deterministic time plus competing PostgreSQL workers for exact equality, delayed timers, double reservation, cancel/assignment races and post-cutoff candidates.
Verify one entry produces one fixed opponent, no hidden approval step, no human/human or same-owner match and no custom-FEN leakage.

tickets.title: Build queue readiness and Stockfish fallback flows
tickets.outcome: Play yourself and Watch your agent play reach an automatic match, with clear readiness and fallback recovery.
scope: Integrate sign-in, selected clock, own-agent readiness and one explicit queue entry with the online workspace.
Failed agent readiness blocks entry and offers Retry or explicit Play yourself. A responsive background owner session remains eligible; a suspended/expired entry needs rejoin.
Prepare browser Stockfish 19 Lite during search. Preparation failure must not block agent matching. At cutoff, offer Retry or Keep searching if the engine is unavailable.
Retry readies the engine and checks for a compatible entry before committing fallback; Keep searching explicitly removes the cutoff.

Run the chosen human/agent seat against identified Stockfish with the same clock, random colors and standard position. Preserve the committed opponent across late events; show cancellation's canonical abort/resign result.
completionEvidence: Exercise readiness failure, background suspension, engine download/startup failure, late readiness and retry/candidate races with synthetic provider traffic.
Demonstrate automatic start, one game per entry, explicit another-game creation and human/agent fallback against the actual browser engine.

tickets.title: Publish allowlisted online history and public replays
tickets.milestone: Public profiles, history and data removal
tickets.outcome: Completed online games have public results and replays with accurate declared control, while private local data stays private.
scope: Project completed friend, queue and fallback games into profiles and public replay URLs. Count each account/game result once; label aborts unscored and exclude local/private/practice saves.
Allow signed-out final replay reads of starting position, accepted moves, time control, result, public participants and declared control metadata. Keep live reads participant-only.
Attribute control/model changes to their accepted moves and terminal actions without relabeling earlier play. Keep compact labels and remove the separate Declared models list.
Allowlist public model names or owner-chosen public labels for custom routing. Do not expose private routing IDs, secret-bearing aliases, connection nicknames, provider traffic or AI conversations.
Describe model and browser Stockfish attribution as declared rather than provider-verified.
completionEvidence: Test idempotent projection/results and every included/excluded game type with signed-out and opponent requests.
Use secret-bearing routing/alias fixtures to prove they never enter public payloads. Exercise replay navigation, mixed control and the removed-list requirement.

tickets.title: Implement account anonymization, explicit replay erasure and safe restore
tickets.milestone: Public profiles, history and data removal
tickets.outcome: Ordinary account deletion anonymizes shared games, while a verified removal request erases shared replays from both histories.
scope: Extend the existing account deletion and encrypted backup/removal-ledger machinery for online tables, public projections and participant snapshots.
Ordinary deletion removes profile, identifying historical snapshots/aliases and service-held private owner data, retaining anonymized shared games as Deleted player.

Explicit verified removal also deletes shared replays from both histories and public URLs. Retain only anonymous opponent result aggregates. Support guest requests through their retained seat ownership credentials.
Remove live service data/projections within 24 hours of verification, and sanitize/remove recovery copies within 30 days. Reapply the newest removal ledger before restored data serves traffic.
Expose clear separate account-deletion and explicit-removal flows, with ownership checks and idempotent processing.
completionEvidence: Exercise account and guest paths, both histories, public URLs, identifying aliases, repeated requests and anonymous opponent totals.
Restore an older backup with a newer removal ledger into an isolated database and prove erased data cannot reappear. Record live/recovery retention scheduling evidence.

tickets.title: Verify integrated online races, recovery and privacy boundaries
tickets.outcome: A reproducible local integration suite proves the shared contracts under competing clients, workers and failures.
scope: Run real Go/PostgreSQL and the pinned rules worker with multiple browser clients and synthetic providers. Include all implemented friend, queue, fallback and removal paths.
Exercise competing matchmakers, late timers, lock waits, duplicate commands, lost receipts, stale tabs/epochs, control changes, uncertain provider work, disconnect claims and service restart.
Verify final-result immutability, continuous clocks, privacy/membership isolation and deletion-safe restore across both clients and public reads.
Publish a case-by-case evidence trace on the tested commit. Keep native accessibility, live-host measurements and rollout outcomes separate from local test results.
completionEvidence: Record reproduction commands, versions/commit and expected/actual outcomes, including failure injection and recovery.
Run the relevant frontend checks, browser integration suite and Go/PostgreSQL tests; mark only scenarios actually exercised with passing evidence.

tickets.title: Verify native desktop accessibility and offline regression
tickets.outcome: The implemented flows work with native desktop keyboard, pointer and screen readers.
scope: Verify real Windows and macOS assistive-technology flows for offline play, friend join, both queue modes, concurrent games, control/recovery, profiles/replay and deletion/removal.
Check board navigation, clocks/status announcements, icon names/tooltips, focus restoration, dialogs and accessible confirmation actions.
Check the existing offline layout and keyboard/history/Undo behavior, short-copy limits, responsive widths and absence of the removed attribution block.
Use the completed MVP accessibility work as a baseline, not acceptance of the new flows. Record unavailable devices or failures honestly.
completionEvidence: Provide native device/OS/browser/screen-reader versions and per-flow results on an identified build.
Resolve material failures or link corrective work before release; screenshots or an automated accessibility scan alone do not pass UX-02.

tickets.title: Verify native mobile touch and screen-reader online play
tickets.outcome: The implemented offline and online flows are usable on iOS and Android with touch and native screen readers.
scope: Run real iOS VoiceOver and Android TalkBack through board play, friend setup/join, both queue choices, concurrent games, agent recovery, replay and privacy actions.
Verify touch targets, icon names, logical focus, dialogs, status/clock announcements and move-history review across phone sizes.
Exercise backgrounding/suspension and reconnect without silent queue re-entry, duplicate provider work or lost game navigation.
Retain the offline layout/behavior, concise interface copy and removal of the separate model list.
completionEvidence: Record device/OS/browser/assistive-technology versions and per-flow outcomes on the tested build.
Demonstrate touch and screen-reader play, including background recovery. Do not substitute viewport emulation for native acceptance.

tickets.title: Verify online hosting, credential isolation and sustainable capacity
tickets.outcome: The existing Vercel/Apache/Go/PostgreSQL host is verified for the new online service before enablement.
scope: Prepare the private Node rules process, additive migrations and least-privilege runtime grants on the existing host. Preserve the direct API path and existing private sync.
On an authorized staging environment, verify Apache flushing, finite SSE renewal/deadlines, poll fallback, CORS/CSP, TLS, auth expiry, private worker reachability and restart recovery.
Audit command/event/replay/log payloads for credentials, raw provider traffic and private routing/identity data. Verify backup coverage and erasure ledger application before restored traffic.
Measure sustainable clients/games, database pool use, CPU, memory, storage and connections. Include slow clients, agent workloads and deadline-worker delay under load.

Document measured limits, monitoring, rollback and overload behavior without adding arbitrary per-owner game/agent caps or promising unmeasured throughput. Use synthetic providers unless separate live usage is authorized.
completionEvidence: Attach actual environment/configuration identifiers, sanitized results, load method and measured bottlenecks.

Demonstrate idle streams do not hold database connections, worker/DB access stays private and restore/removal protections still work. Record missing authorization or host constraints instead of claiming unrun checks.

tickets.title: Complete online acceptance handoff and opt-in friend rollout
tickets.outcome: An evidence-backed, reversible opt-in friend release can be enabled after the recorded release decision.
scope: Reconcile all 60 implementation scenarios with the preceding tickets, including native device, host/capacity, privacy/removal and recovery evidence. Keep UX-01 and REL-01 recorded as prior planning approvals.
Prepare the release candidate, feature enablement, monitoring, rollback and support/runbook handoff. Keep public queue disabled during the first friend cohort.
Present the concrete release packet for the separate approval required by the agreed specification. Creating this backlog or approving the prototype does not supply that approval.
After that recorded approval, enable the opt-in friend cohort and record actual join/play/reconnect/result/history/removal outcomes. Stop or roll back on material failures.
completionEvidence: Publish the acceptance ledger and release decision with the exact commit/configuration.
Record rollout observations and rollback readiness. Leave this ticket open while approval, required evidence or enablement remains outstanding.

tickets.title: Enable public agent matchmaking after friend rollout review
tickets.outcome: Public agent matchmaking is enabled only after the friend cohort and queue-specific operating evidence are accepted.
scope: Review the opt-in friend cohort and resolve material findings. Reconfirm compatible pairing, one automatic game per explicit entry, unlimited explicit concurrency and cutoff/fallback behavior on the release candidate.
Check readiness failures, Stockfish preparation, offline runners, provider uncertainty and measured host headroom with no platform-funded AI usage.
Prepare the concrete public-queue enablement and rollback packet, and obtain the separate public-queue release decision required by the approved handoff.
After approval, enable the queue and monitor assignments, cutoffs, failures, fallback and capacity. Preserve friend/offline operation during rollback.
completionEvidence: Record the public-queue release decision, enabled configuration and tested commit.
Capture actual queue/fallback/concurrent-game outcomes and operating observations; do not mark deployment complete from planning or local simulation alone.
